kids.text: Oryx eyes between al-Rusafa and the bridge
have brought me love by ways I know and ways I don't.
They brought back my old longing, though I had
never got over it: they heaped embers on embers.
They came away unhurt and left hearts to ruin,
as if pierced by the tips of straight brown spears.
They told us, “We are new moons: we only
light the night traveller's way, and offer him no food.”
No gift but what an eye takes away for the road,
no union but with the phantom that comes by night.
Just when they had shaken my heart from its place
and set fire to all between my ribs and breast,
they turned away, as a drinker turns from wine
once he has had his fill, for fear of getting drunk.
Why did they not, before grey hair showed, start me
on plain despair, or turn to betrayal then?
If they have changed, or denied a pledge they gave,

kids.text: There was nothing to bring back: the old love was still burning, and they added to the fire.
